name: Pickerel Lake (Otsego) State Forest Campground
evidence: Esri + NAIP z18 at 45.1780,-84.5180: loop roads and pad clearings sit 35-50 m east of Pickerel Lake behind a continuous forest strip, 3-4 m above it (3DEP 282-284 vs 279). The gravel ramp is the only open frontage. FCFS, no DNR site map; 'sandy shoreline' is prose

name: Pigeon Bridge State Forest Campground
evidence: OSM campground outline + NAIP/Esri at 45.1570,-84.4655: the 10-site loop is north of Sturgeon Valley Rd, 40-65 m east of the ~8 m Pigeon River through forest, ~4 m above it (3DEP 281.5-282 vs 277.5). Canopy-blind; FCFS with no DNR site map, so default down

name: Pine Lake Campground
evidence: NAIP + Esri at 44.1957,-86.0092: 12-site loop (OSM) in full canopy; its east end runs ~10-20 m from the shore, but no pad is visible and the spur to the water is the picnic/beach access. FS page is prose; FCFS, not on rec.gov, no site map. Unconfirmable, so default down

name: Platte River State Forest Campground
evidence: Esri + NAIP at 44.6440,-85.9810: the visible pad clearings are 80-90 m from the Platte River through hardwood canopy, and the loop's south leg ~40 m back behind a treeline (3DEP pads 198 vs river 196.4). 'Accessible by water' is the canoe landing path. FCFS, no DNR site map

name: Pigeon River State Forest Campground
evidence: Leaf-off Esri at 45.1767,-84.4293 + NAIP: a pad clearing at the river bend (45.17676,-84.42925; a tent/camper on it in NAIP) runs to within ~10-15 m of the bank, ~1.3 m above the water (3DEP 270.0 vs 268.7). The Pigeon is ~7-9 m wide, so creekside not riverfront

name: Pine Grove State Forest Campground
evidence: Leaf-off Esri + NAIP at 45.2446,-84.4459: the main site clearing sits on a terrace ~5 m above the Pigeon River (3DEP 249.9 vs 244.4), ~30 m back behind a conifer belt. The other pads are under canopy farther east, beyond the floodplain meadow. No view or shoreline pad shown; FCFS, no site map

name: Rainbow Bend State Forest Campground
evidence: Esri at 44.6704,-84.4188: the 7-site drive-in loop is ~165-200 m from the Au Sable River through forest; re-pinned from the access track onto the loop. The open riverbank clearing with tables (OSM 'Lower Rainbow Bend') is the DNR's canoe group-use area, not RV sites

name: Pretty Lake State Forest Campground
evidence: NAIP + Esri at 46.6027,-85.6568: drive-in pads along the NE shore sit ~5-20 m from the water, e.g. a dirt pad at 46.6022,-85.6570 and a white trailer at 46.6029,-85.6574, with paths to the water, <1 m above the lake (3DEP 230.8-231.5 vs 230.4). The walk-in sites 19-26 are elsewhere
